10. API Endpoints for Modules

10.1 When does a module need its own API endpoints?

Simple modules that only display static content do not need their own endpoints. API endpoints are necessary for:

  • Loading dynamic data from the database
  • Saving forms (POST)
  • Executing actions (file upload, sending email)
  • Status updates (polling)

10.2 Creating an endpoint

API endpoints go into apps/abpe_ui/api/components/ or directly into views.py. For modular endpoints, we recommend a separate file:

# apps/abpe_ui/api/components/mein_modul_api.py
from django.http import JsonResponse
from rest_framework.decorators import api_view, permission_classes
from rest_framework.permissions import IsAuthenticated

@api_view(['GET'])
@permission_classes([IsAuthenticated])
def get_data(request):
    """
    GET /api/mein-modul/data/
    Provides data for the module.
    """
    data = {
        'items': [
            {'id': 1, 'name': 'Entry 1', 'value': 42},
            {'id': 2, 'name': 'Entry 2', 'value': 17},
        ],
        'total': 2
    }
    return JsonResponse(data)

@api_view(['POST'])
@permission_classes([IsAuthenticated])
def save_data(request):
    """
    POST /api/mein-modul/save/
    Saves data.
    """
    import json
    try:
        body = json.loads(request.body)
        name = body.get('name', '').strip()
        if not name:
            return JsonResponse({'success': False, 'error': 'Name missing'}, status=400)
        # ... Save logic ...
        return JsonResponse({'success': True, 'id': 99})
    except Exception as e:
        return JsonResponse({'success': False, 'error': str(e)}, status=500)

10.3 Registering URLs

In urls.py — before the generic routes at the end:

# In urls.py — after the existing API routes
from .api.components.mein_modul_api import get_data, save_data

# In urlpatterns — BEFORE the generic <str:module_id>/ routes:
path('api/mein-modul/data/',  get_data,   name='mm_data'),
path('api/mein-modul/save/',  save_data,  name='mm_save'),

10.4 GET request in module JS

async function loadData() {
    try {
        const resp = await fetch('/api/mein-modul/data/');

        if (!resp.ok) {
            console.error('HTTP error:', resp.status);
            return;
        }

        const data = await resp.json();
        renderItems(data.items);

    } catch(e) {
        console.error('Network error:', e);
    }
}

10.5 POST request with CSRF

All POST requests need the CSRF token from the cookie:

function getCsrf() {
    return document.cookie.split(';')
        .map(c => c.trim())
        .find(c => c.startsWith('csrftoken='))
        ?.split('=')[1] || '';
}

async function saveData(payload) {
    try {
        const resp = await fetch('/api/mein-modul/save/', {
            method:  'POST',
            headers: {
                'Content-Type': 'application/json',
                'X-CSRFToken':  getCsrf()
            },
            body: JSON.stringify(payload)
        });

        const data = await resp.json();

        if (data.success) {
            console.log('Saved, ID:', data.id);
        } else {
            console.error('Error:', data.error);
        }

    } catch(e) {
        console.error('Network error:', e);
    }
}

10.6 Using existing endpoints

The portal already offers many endpoints that can be used in modules:

EndpointMethodDescription
/api/stats/GETStatistics (consultants, emails, projects)
